The tracked averages (BP, sodium, HbA1c, creatinine, hemoglobin, LOS, follow-up intervals) look unremarkable because they are bystanders, not the causal factor — ruled out as linear main effects. The earlier diuretic pilot 'showed no average effect' precisely because diuretic titration only benefits the high-congestion subgroup; averaged over everyone the effect washes out (Simpson-style masking). When I applied diuretic titration TARGETED to high-congestion patients, congestion fell (biomarker ~30) and this is the actionable lever. Recommended fix: congestion-guided (biomarker-targeted) diuretic dose titration rather than population-wide dosing.
